clue.text: Spots rook by tree

blocks.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a rook perched beside a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb meaning sees, but it is a noun: an outbreak of spots on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of red spots or blotches on the skin.

clue.text: Check if one's popped in to lie down

indicators.note: something popped in has been slipped inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: to rest is to lie down
one is I, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether a person has dropped by for a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' must be read as 'one is', so both the numeral and the verb go in.
explanation.definitionFit: To check an advance is to resist or hold it back; the words are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Toil over an advertising jingle

blocks.note: to slog is to toil hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A copywriter labours long over a catchy advertising tune.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a catchy advertising phrase, close kin to a jingle as a memorable marketing line.

clue.text: White-bearded old man seen round river port in Colombia

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: Santa Claus is pictured as a white-bearded old man
the setter's source for these letters is unclear; no standard crossword sense of seen gives them
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An elderly bearded traveller spotted near a river in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Only SANTA and the river letter are firmly clued; the rest is best taken from the definition. Colombia's best-known Caribbean port is Santa Marta, which this key does not print.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is given as a place name in Colombia, a coastal town reached from the Caribbean; the key names it as the port.

clue.text: Member blowing hard, a jazz trumpeter

blocks.note: an arm is a limb, or member, of the body
a wind blowing hard is a strong one

explanation.surface: A band member puffing away hard on a jazz trumpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing hard' fits a trumpeter so well it seems part of the definition, but it describes a strong wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong was the celebrated New Orleans jazz trumpeter and singer.

clue.text: Opinion expressed by English under canvas?

indicators.note: being under canvas means staying inside a tent, so the letter sits within the shelter word

blocks.note: a tent is made of canvas
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English camper airing views from inside a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under canvas' is the everyday idiom for camping, so the letter goes inside the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, which is a settled opinion.

clue.text: Maiden on important operation in Marx Brothers film

blocks.note: M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written
something key is important
a business is a commercial operation

explanation.surface: A young woman undergoing a major operation, as if in a comic film.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey Business is the 1931 Marx Brothers comedy set aboard an ocean liner.

clue.text: Electrical supply system — phone chap about one

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: to ring someone is to phone them
a chap is a man
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man rings an electrician about a power problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring main is the looped household wiring circuit that supplies the sockets, typical in British homes.

clue.text: Springboks, say — see 27 run with long bounding strides

definitions.note: plural, but antelope can serve as its own plural

blocks.note: 27 across is a stake in poker
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: South African rugby players running with long strides.
explanation.walkthrough: The Springboks are South Africa's rugby team, which tempts a sporting reading, but a springbok is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The springbok is a species of gazelle, so springboks are an example of the animal family named.

clue.text: Sober, lad fell in hectic plant

indicators.note: hectic means frantic and disorderly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sober young man nonetheless tripped in a frantic scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells of Ireland is a garden plant with green bell-shaped calyces, a type of flowering annual.

clue.text: Mouthpiece for cyclists?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who speaks on behalf of a group
setter's reading: a bicycle wheel has wire rods radiating from the hub, so a man of those rods suits cyclists

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after its sixth letter: wheels have spokes, so a man of spokes is the voice of cyclists.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesman is a person who speaks officially for a group, its public voice.

clue.text: Not one tenor in group of singers

blocks.note: not one is none
T is an abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A choir with no tenor among its members.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine performers, such as nine singers.

clue.text: Immoral boy in group

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a set is a group
Carl is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A badly behaved lad in a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet has the old sense of sinful or immoral, as in a scarlet woman.

clue.text: Some weather — Malvern is hot!

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters sit inside a longer run

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A weather report from the English town of Malvern announcing heat.
explanation.walkthrough: Malvern is a spa town in Worcestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal means relating to heat, so a thermal spring is a hot one.

clue.text: Low character

blocks.note: surface reading: a person of base or vulgar nature
setter's reading: a cartoon figure created by David Low, the newspaper cartoonist

explanation.walkthrough: Low is the surname of the New Zealand-born cartoonist whose pompous, reactionary army officer became a byword in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure is a fictional cartoon creation of David Low, so he is literally that artist's character.

clue.text: Girl in hospital department attempting to avoid confrontation

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
Mollie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nurse in a hospital ward trying to keep the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Emollient literally means soothing to skin, and figuratively calming and conciliatory in manner.

clue.text: Pair allowed in band

blocks.note: a brace is a pair, especially of game birds
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Two musicians permitted to join a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks musical, but it is a ring worn round the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band or chain worn on the wrist.

clue.text: Struggle to gain possession in game

blocks.note: first meaning: to scramble or grope for something
second meaning: the word-building board game with letter tiles

explanation.surface: Players fighting over the ball during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a scrambling grab for something, and it is also the trademarked word board game.

clue.text: Toy with herrings cook cooked

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene where the cook has prepared some herrings.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocking horse is a child's wooden horse on rockers, a classic plaything.

clue.text: Fish following ferryman

blocks.note: the char is a fish of the trout family
on can mean following, as in 'later on'

explanation.surface: A fish swimming behind a ferryman's boat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Charon rows the souls of the dead across the river Styx, the underworld's boatman.

clue.text: Poles over Spain, thinly dispersed

blocks.note: spars are poles, as on a ship
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Polish people scattered across Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' tempts N and S, but here it is the word for wooden rods; in a down clue 'over' sets it above the Spain letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means scanty and spread thinly over an area.

clue.text: Meal in not entirely warm French country house

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the final letter is cut
in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: chaud is French for warm
tea is an afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: Dining at a not-quite-heated manor in rural France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' serves twice: it tells you the word for warm is French, and it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A château is a French castle or large country residence.

clue.text: Before jaunt, I loaded cases

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the clue words wrap around the letters wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Before a trip, someone packed luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Until means up to the time of, so it can stand for before, as in 'not until noon'.

clue.text: A friendly ball may make you have a strong desire to dance

blocks.note: to long for something is to have a strong desire for it
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: An invitation to a sociable dance that leaves you eager to go.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a long hop is a short, badly pitched delivery that is easy to hit, so it is friendly to the batsman; 'ball' looks like a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket term names a poor delivery that gives the batsman an easy scoring chance, hence generous or friendly.

clue.text: Sign made by one supporter after fifth of tackles

indicators.note: fifth of picks out the letter in fifth position of the following word

blocks.note: the fifth letter of tackles
I is the Roman numeral one
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A rugby supporter's banner after a tackling display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the tackles letter first, followed by the one and the supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Club official, someone much valued at end of year

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: a valued person is called a treasure
the last letter of year

explanation.surface: A club honouring a cherished member at its year-end dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer who manages a club's or society's funds.

clue.text: What a surveyor might use, the one in Toledo possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the words may be arranged some other way

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A surveyor in the Spanish city of Toledo picking out the tool he might need.
explanation.definitionFit: A theodolite is a surveyor's instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles.

clue.text: Stake required, unlimited

indicators.note: unlimited means without limits, so the word loses its outer edges

blocks.note: wanted means required

explanation.surface: A gambler is told the bet has no upper limit.
explanation.walkthrough: WANTED loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker an ante is the stake each player puts in before the deal.
